# Non-Root Sidecar Scripts: `node:*-alpine` and Friends

When a Pod's `securityContext` enforces non-root execution
(`runAsNonRoot: true` + `runAsUser: <uid>`, e.g. uid 10001), the script
that runs inside a `node:22-alpine` (or any `node:*-alpine`) container has
two recurring constraints:

1. `npm install -g <pkg>` fails because the default prefix and default
   cache resolve to root-owned paths.
2. `apk add <pkg>` requires root and is unavailable, so the script must
   stick to what the stock image ships.

## Rule 1: Set `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` and `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE` before `npm install`

Two distinct failures collapse into one fix:

- Default install prefix `/usr/local/lib/node_modules` is root-owned;
  non-root uids cannot write. Symptom: `EACCES` on the install step.
- Default cache resolves to `$HOME/.npm`, but `HOME` is unset by default in
  the container, so npm falls back to `/.npm` — also unwritable by
  non-root. Specific symptom: `npm error path /.npm`, `npm error errno
  EACCES`, `npm error Your cache folder contains root-owned files`.

Script preamble for any non-root node-based sidecar:

```sh
export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/tmp/npm-global
export NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/tmp/npm-cache
export PATH=$NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX/bin:$PATH
mkdir -p "$NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX" "$NPM_CONFIG_CACHE"
npm install -g <package>
```

`/tmp` is world-writable in the stock image. If the workload sets
`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, mount an `emptyDir` over `/tmp` or pick a
different prefix under a writable volume.

## Rule 2: Restrict the script to commands the stock image ships

`apk add` needs root; in a non-root sidecar it returns
`ERROR: Unable to lock database: Permission denied`. The script must use
only what `node:*-alpine` already provides:

- `wget` (busybox) — not `curl`. Curl is not in `node:22-alpine`.
- `awk`, `sh`, `mkdir`, `cat`, `printf` — all busybox builtins.
- POSIX shell arithmetic with truncated values — not `bc`. `bc` is not in
  `node:22-alpine`.

Truncating floats for POSIX arithmetic uses parameter expansion (see
[knowledgebase/observability/exposition-format-consumption.md](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase/blob/main/observability/exposition-format-consumption.md)).

## When to apply

- Any sidecar that runs in a Pod where the container `securityContext`
  sets `runAsNonRoot: true` or `runAsUser` to a non-zero uid.
- PodSecurity `restricted` namespaces, which force non-root by policy.
- Any time the script must function without elevation in a hardened
  cluster.

## When skipping is acceptable

- Sidecars that run as root by explicit decision (e.g., legacy workloads
  that have a documented exception from PodSecurity policy). Even there,
  prefer the non-root recipe so the script survives a future security
  tightening without rework.
